episodes.173123: Significant clearing late in the morning resulted in the development of high instability across eastern Utah. This, paired with upper level support and ample moisture, produced strong to severe thunderstorms across the area in the late afternoon and early evening hours. Significant hail accumulation occurred in Green River and along I-70. Additionally, heavy rain occurred with storms which led to flash flooding across portions of Grand County.
episodes.173124: Significant clearing late in the morning resulted in the development of high instability across western Colorado. This, paired with upper level support and ample moisture, produced strong to severe thunderstorms across the area in the late afternoon and early evening hours. Severe wind gusts up to 61 mph occurred in Garfield County. Additionally, heavy rain occurred with storms which led to flash flooding and debris flows across portions of San Miguel, Montrose, and Mesa counties.
episodes.174055: A main low pressure centered over southeastern Idaho had several shortwaves rotating around the base of the low and cross through Arizona. This brought showers and thunderstorms over portions of northern Arizona.
episodes.174109: A strong and occasionally severe thunderstorm moved through parts of Boulder and Weld Counties producing large hail during the afternoon of October 1st. The storm went on to produce strong, damaging winds near in Washington County later in the afternoon.
episodes.174164: A cold front reached Kauai on October 2.  The rain band associated with the front generated the wettest day of the month for Kauai, with 3 to 5 inches occurring mainly along the north-facing slopes. This enhanced rainfall did not cause significant flooding problems.
episodes.174776: The combination of an approaching trough, increasing moisture from the Caribbean, a light southeast wind flow and local effects resulted in several active days across Puerto Rico. These factors enhanced the afternoon showers and thunderstorms for a few days. Additionally, the soils remained saturated from the rains in September, so several mudslides and flooding reports were received.
episodes.174871: At the beginning of October, storms brought severe hail and flash flooding to portions of southern Utah.

events.narrative: The river gauge on Havasu creek near the Colorado River rose 6.7 feet in 15 minutes between 1130 and 1145 PM MST. The river gauge is below/downstream from the Village of Supai. The flood damaged all six bridges in and around Supai Village, some of which were a total loss. The main foot and mule trail to the village was damaged and in need of repair. This 8 mile trail is the only way to the village from a road other than by helicopter.
Local stream gauges recorded some initial rises in response to enhanced rainfall rates, but receded quickly without much impact as rains diminished quickly over the area.
Emergency Managers reported that the yards of several houses  in El Polvorin, Dorado were flooded due to heavy rain.
An ex-employee from the NWS reported flooding along Road PR-22, Intersection with Road PR-142 in Dorado. Three cars were affected by the flooding.
A social media user reported flooding along Road  PR-604, in direction to San Jose, Los Rabanos. The road was impassable.
Emergency Managers reported flooding along Sector Espinosa in Higuillar. The water managed to get inside the houses.
Emergency Managers reported that Road PR-694, near Sector Los Torres was impassable de to heavy rainfall.
An Anasazi State Park employee reported 1 inch diameter hail at the Anasazi State Park Museum.
A resident reported quarter-sized hail that dented cars in Hanksville.
Debris as a result of heavy rain from thunderstorms was cleared off I-70 between mile markers 168 and 170 from both the eastbound and westbound lanes.
Several inches to over a foot of dime-sized hail accumulated in Green River and along adjacent portions of I-70.

More than 50 people were stranded overnight in Grand County, Utah after heavy rain from severe thunderstorms wiped out a portion of Mineral Bottom Road which led to a remote boat ramp. The rain completed demolished a section of switchbacks with large boulders accumulating.
Pictures from social media shared by broadcast media showed hail damage from Cedar City to Enoch. The largest hail was estimated to be ping pong ball-sized.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding on Sulphur Creek.
Flash flooding occurred as a result of heavy rain from thunderstorms on the lower end of the No Thoroughfare Trail between D Road and Monument Road in Grand Junction.
The Fort Pearce Wash gauge peaked at 789 cfs.

Numerous roads were closed in Spanish Valley due to flash flooding as a result of heavy rain from thunderstorms. This included Shumway Lane and Old City Park, Floy, Hastings, Sunny Acres, and Kerby Roads. Roads remained closed overnight. The Pack Creek gauge on Pack Creek Road reported a rise of 4 feet when about an inch of rain fell in 90 minutes.
